summary.headline: Cipla Q1 FY27 revenue INR7,119 crore (+2% YoY reported, ~4% adjusted); EBITDA margin ex-other income 16.7%, FY27 18.5–20% guidance kept.
summary.overview: Cipla reported its highest-ever Q1 revenue of INR7,119 crore, up 2% YoY, but a new accounting presentation (certain marketing and promotional expenses now netted from revenue from 1 April 2026) depresses reported growth; management says adjusted growth is about 4%. EBITDA margin excluding other income was 16.7% and reported gross margin after material cost was 62.5%, hit by product mix, war-related costs, and higher-than-normal inventory write-offs. Management kept the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20% and reiterated a US$1 billion North America exit run-rate, contingent on launches of Ventolin, three respiratory assets (including generic Advair) and one large peptide. The company is moving into a new CFO transition, with Dinesh Jain succeeding Ashish Adukia as Global CFO.

financial_highlights.change: +2% YoY reported; ~4% adjusted for the presentation change

financial_highlights.value: INR9,494 crore (debt incl. leases INR600 crore) as of 30 June 2026
financial_highlights.change: After INR1,050 crore dividend paid this quarter

segments.name: One India
segments.commentary: Highest-ever quarterly revenue with 12% YoY growth; branded prescription business grew 15.4% per IQVIA, and chronic mix rose to 60.4%. Yurpeak (tirzepatide) contributed about INR80 crore, roughly 1.5 points of growth, and the INR100-plus crore club now has 33 brands.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of US$162 million; Cipla holds 21% share of the US albuterol MDI market. Generic Ventolin launched after approval last quarter, with commercial shipments started and volumes ramping toward year-end.

segments.name: South Africa
segments.commentary: Private-market secondary sales grew 6.5% vs market 5.7% (IQVIA MAT); reported rupee revenue fell about 5% largely due to presentation change and loss of a tender whose supply plan continues to weigh this year.

segments.name: EMEU
segments.commentary: 5% YoY growth in USD terms, driven by DTM and B2B execution, with margin stability maintained.

segments.name: Consumer Health
segments.commentary: Nicotex, Omnigel and Cipladine hold number 1 positions; consumer wellness India revenue was roughly INR480 crore vs INR470 crore a year ago, with management citing a strong prior-year base and the presentation change in South Africa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other income) guidance of 18.5–20% broadly unchanged; management says it is predicated on new launches and margin improvement.

North America: US$1 billion exit run-rate retained, dependent on approval and launch timing of Ventolin, three respiratory assets (including generic Advair) and one large peptide; management said the approvals give line of sight to that exit rate.
Gross margin expected to improve from Q3 as recipe mix rises; new launches carry healthy margins to replace high-margin prior-year products.
War-related cost impact estimated at 1–2% of revenue; PLI incentives accrue on sales of PLI molecules and will be phased into later quarters, with almost none booked in Q1.
Lanreotide US supply not included in Q4 projections; remediation at Pharmathene and a US tech-transfer site run in parallel with timing dependent on regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Capex increased and directed to organic growth, R&D and biosimilars; small capital deployed to in-licensing and acquisitions in US and Europe.

US manufacturing facilities filed two of the three respiratory assets; the third was filed from Goa, which has been audited and cleared (Verna facility classified VAI after routine GMP inspection and PAI this quarter).
Invagen (New York) routine GMP inspection concluded with one Form 483 observation, expected to affect only smaller solid-oral launches; Indore reinspection expected soon.
Invagen Unit 1 (Advair-linked) inspection in February with two observations; approval expected any time per management.
No significant field-force additions planned this year; about 12,000 MRs.
demand_pricing: Respiratory grew 15%, anti-diabetes 43%, cardiac 20% and urology double-digit (IQVIA, quarter to June 2026); chronic portfolio growth driven by volume.
Yurpeak (tirzepatide) is number two in the overall IPM category behind Mounjaro; monthly sales growing, with management saying generics coexist with the innovator brand.
Ventolin: exclusivity for about six months; management expects to capture generic share until competition enters, and sees Advair facing three or four competitors so not a US$100 million product.
South Africa tender business declined; private market growth ahead of market, with currency movements hedged and affecting reported figures.
Acute portfolio tracking the market in line, while respiratory and some chronic segments outperform.

qa_highlights.question: How has the accounting change affected growth, especially India and South Africa?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Adukia said adjusted total growth is about 4% versus reported 2%; the adjustment is primarily in South Africa and the company did not split it by market.

qa_highlights.question: Does the US$1 billion exit run-rate remain, and is the peptide pipeline still four products?
qa_highlights.answer: Achin Gupta said the pipeline is three respiratory assets plus one large peptide, with other peptides in the approval queue; approvals of these give line of sight to the US$1 billion exit rate.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 18.5–20% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish Adukia said it is broadly unchanged, but risk exists if launches are delayed; the plan includes launch and margin-improvement assumptions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory write-off impact and war-related cost on gross margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said war-related costs are about 1–2% of revenue; the inventory charge was above normal but was not quantified, and it sits within COGS.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin below pre-Revlimid levels and where is the margin going?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin is below steady state due to launch opex already committed in manpower and facilities, temporary war costs, and lagging new product revenue; a gradual sequential improvement is expected, with no FY28 guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: How will the cash pile be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex for organic growth, R&D and biosimilars, in-licensing with upfront payments, and conservative small acquisitions in US and Europe; no large deal announced.

risks_watch: Delay in US approvals (Advair-related respiratory assets, peptide) could push back the US$1 billion exit run-rate and the 18.5–20% EBITDA margin guidance.
War-related cost headwind of 1–2% of revenue and unquantified inventory write-offs; gross margin trajectory depends on product mix.
South Africa tender losses continue to dent reported revenue through the coming quarters.
Ventolin ramp-up is gated to around year-end; generic competition may enter after the six-month exclusivity.
Lanreotide US supply timing is uncertain and excluded from Q4 projections; Invagen Form 483 observation and Indore reinspection to be cleared.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and launch pipeline (highest Q1 revenue, market-leading India chronic growth), but cautious and evasive on margin trajectory and US timing, repeatedly tying outcomes to approvals and declining to guide FY28 margins. Several answers on segment-level growth were deferred, with management citing IQVIA data instead.

Right now, the -- what you saw last quarter and this quarter is not our steady state

growth.why: FY27 EBITDA margin (ex-other income) guidance of 18.5–20% held and US$1 billion North America exit run-rate reiterated, dependent on launches of Ventolin, three respiratory assets and one large peptide; reported Q1 revenue +2% (about 4% adjusted for presentation change), with the approvals giving 'line of sight' but no quantified capacity or timelines per launch.
